policy.foreign_suffix: foreign compiler tools and environment remain explicit assumptions

claim.statement: For a supported source program, configuration, and stated resource/environment premises, every completed target observation is allowed by the executable source semantics.
preconditions: The source bytes and source graph are the identified inputs.
The program is accepted by the published lexical, parsing, checking, ownership, effect, and contract rules.
Numeric, target, scheduler, stack, allocation, and fuel premises are recorded for the run.
Foreign libraries, foreign compiler tools, operating-system behavior, and external services satisfy their named contracts.
A target may report only the resource failures permitted by the stated resource law; safe Jet has no C-style undefined-behavior escape.
trusted_components: ratified Jet language and Core specifications
the executable model implementation and its checked source inputs
the pinned checker identity from jet.compiler-proof.v1
named foreign compiler, runtime, operating-system, and environment contracts
unsupported_cases: unmodeled Core receiver or adapter behavior
unbounded scheduling, concurrency, or progress claims
unverified FFI, ABI/layout, foreign library, or browser behavior
a source, candidate, checker, configuration, or proof artifact whose identity changed

binding_methods.construction: closed executable transition relation checked by this contract checker
binding_methods.limit: model validity and correspondence to the full Jet implementation are not inferred
the bounded slice does not establish direct verification of every production stage
finite bounded agreement is tested evidence, never universal preservation

proven: The checker validates this contract's shape and disjoint proof-boundary labels.
The finite witness relation is deterministically serialized and compared with the canonical ordered-effects observation relation.
Incomplete obligations, identity drift, discarded cases, mismatches, unknown statuses, and unavailable replay cannot qualify as proof.
assumed: The ratified language and Core specifications state the intended Jet semantics; if those specifications differ from the checker encoding, this contract proves conformance to the encoding rather than to the language.
The candidate compiler construction and foreign compiler/environment suffix satisfy their named contracts.
The pinned jet.compiler-proof.v1 claim identity identifies the candidate without changing its meaning.
tested: The retained value, mutation, compile-time, input/result, rejection, typed-failure, cleanup, and resource witnesses agree between the independent model and implementation.
A deliberately wrong observation and each independent wrong-rule witness are rejected as mismatch and cannot be promoted to matched.
When requested, each live Jet mapping is attempted only as identity-bound observation evidence; unobserved dimensions remain explicitly unproved.
blocked: Universal preservation for all Jet-controlled parsing, checking, comptime, lowering, optimization, Core, runtime, and adapter stages.
Live Lean replay of the candidate proof artifact when the pinned checker is unavailable.

Complete fresh AOT, resident JIT, interpreter, and web conformance evidence for the language corpus, including identity-bound observations across every applicable stage and adapter, remains unrecorded.

Complete implementation-bound mappings for every observation dimension, especially typed failure, mutation, input trace, ordered effects, cleanup, resource premises, scheduler traces, and allowed schedules.

coverage.owner_rule: every generated row has a non-empty rule, live owner, and explicit uncovered state until a checked argument exists
coverage.qualification_rule: model agreement is tested evidence; a denominator row is proved only after complete identity-bound Jet observations and no current mapping may claim that state
